## Structure and components

- [statement] The ASPro-PD protocol gives the primary outcome as the combined score of parts I, II, and III of the MDS-UPDRS, whereas the Cure Parkinson's trial page says the MDS-UPDRS Part III rating scale will be used to measure changes in motor symptoms. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12916515/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/research/research-projects/ambroxol/
- [statement] In MOVES-PD part 2, 221 participants were randomly assigned to venglustat (n=110) or placebo (n=111), and the absolute difference between groups in the MDS-UPDRS parts II and III combined score was 2·58 (95% CI -1·10 to 6·27; p=0·17). (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37479372/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The Mullin et al. ambroxol trial in PD was a single-center open-label noncontrolled clinical trial in which 18 patients completed the study, with escalating oral ambroxol up to 1.26 g per day. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6990847/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/research/research-projects/ambroxol/
- [statement] In the open-label Mullin trial, the authors report that CSF GCase activity decreased by 19% while CSF α-synuclein concentration increased by 13%. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6990847/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies
- [statement] The ASPro-PD protocol reports that approximately 10–15% of individuals with PD carry a GBA1 variant, and a Movement Disorders review reports 5%–10% in Asian and approximately 10%–15% in European populations. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12916515/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13518287/
- [statement] Bial's ACTIVATE phase 2 study was announced as testing two fixed-dose levels of BIA 28-6156 (10mg and 60mg/day), an allosteric activator of GCase, against placebo, with clinical progression assessed for up to 78 weeks of double-blind treatment. (medium confidence) — https://www.biospace.com/bial-r-and-amp-d-announces-first-patient-dosed-in-its-phase-2-clinical-trial-of-bia-28-6156-to-treat-parkinson-s-disease-patients-with-a-pathogenic-variant-in-the-glucocerebrosidase-gba1-gene · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://www.clinicaltrialsarena.com/news/bial-rd-first-patient-bia-28-6156/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In the open-label noncontrolled Mullin trial, scores on part 3 of the Movement Disorders Society Unified Parkinson Disease Rating Scale decreased (ie, improved) by 6.8 points. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6990847/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/research/research-projects/ambroxol/
- [statement] In a 52-week phase 2 randomised trial of ambroxol in Parkinson disease dementia, 55 patients were randomised and the authors report no evidence to suggest differences between groups on primary or secondary outcomes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-01) — https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamaneurology/fullarticle/2835760 · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://lbda.org/trial-results-ambroxol-safe-in-pdd-but-no-clear-evidence-of-benefit, https://www.neurologylive.com/view/randomized-trial-highlights-uncertainties-ambroxol-improve-cognition-parkinson-disease-dementia
- [statement] Secondary reports on the Parkinson disease dementia ambroxol trial note that the sample size for GBA1 variant carriers was too small to say for certain that apparent improvements were real, and they list recruiting more GBA1 carriers for future studies. (medium confidence) — https://lbda.org/trial-results-ambroxol-safe-in-pdd-but-no-clear-evidence-of-benefit · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://www.neurologylive.com/view/randomized-trial-highlights-uncertainties-ambroxol-improve-cognition-parkinson-disease-dementia
- [statement] The registry record for NCT07011771, the Capsida Biotherapeutics Phase 1/2 trial of CAP-003 gene therapy in GBA1 associated Parkinson's disease, lists the status as WITHDRAWN, with the stated reason that a protocol stopping rule was met for a separate trial of a different disease state and therapy using similar technology. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT07011771 · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MOVES-PD, which evaluated the glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor venglustat, was described as unsuccessful in a Movement Disorders review, and its authors report that venglustat showed no beneficial treatment effect compared with placebo. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13518287/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37479372/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Mullin et al. report that ambroxol was detected in cerebrospinal fluid, with a 156-ng/mL increase in the level of ambroxol in CSF between days 0 and 186. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6990847/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12916515/
- [statement] The ASPro-PD protocol describes a phase 3, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of high-dose ambroxol that will enrol 330 PD patients with confirmed GBA1 status. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12916515/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/research/research-projects/ambroxol/
- [statement] ASPro-PD, a phase 3 ambroxol trial, was initiated in 2025. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13518287/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://cureparkinsons.org.uk/research/research-projects/ambroxol/
- [statement] A Movement Disorders review reports that in one analysis of 395 PD patients without GBA1 variants, approximately one‐third showed decreased GCase activity comparable with that observed in GBA1 variant carriers. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13518287/ · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12916515/
- [statement] Bial reports that the phase 2b ACTIVATE study of BIA 28-6156 (pariceract) in patients with a pathogenic GBA1 variant did not meet its primary, nor the key secondary, efficacy endpoint, and that Bial decided to discontinue further development of BIA 28-6156 for this indication. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-12) — https://www.bial.com/en/media/news/bial-reports-topline-results-from-activate-phase-2b-study-in-gba-associated-parkinsons · keywords: GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies · also: https://www.neurologylive.com/view/pariceract-fails-meet-primary-end-point-phase-2b-activate-trial-gba1-associated-pd

## Research summary — GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies

GBA1 variants are among the most common genetic risk factors for Parkinson's disease, so drugs aimed at the GCase lysosomal pathway have been tested as possible disease-modifying treatments. An open-label phase 2 ambroxol trial reported CSF penetration. Three later randomised trials reported no benefit on their primary outcomes: venglustat (MOVES-PD), ambroxol in Parkinson disease dementia, and Bial's BIA 28-6156 (ACTIVATE), which Bial then discontinued. The phase 3 ambroxol trial ASPro-PD was initiated in 2025. The registry lists the CAP-003 gene therapy trial as withdrawn. This is a research summary, not clinical advice.

## Source disagreement — GBA1, ambroxol and lysosomal-targeted therapies

Mullin et al. cite reports that ambroxol increases GCase enzyme activity, yet measured a 19% decrease in CSF GCase activity alongside a 35% increase in CSF GCase protein levels.

Gate verdict: `SUPPORTED`. Auxiliary assertion: `prose:0eecb03b37193700405fe3ec34e87c46b887a3ca14628c6357e195225456fa70`. Statement hash: `0eecb03b37193700405fe3ec34e87c46b887a3ca14628c6357e195225456fa70`.
